overall: The AG found the Committee violated the OML by holding Aug. 19, 2025 meetings in an inaccessible location and by omitting posting date and time from original and amended notices; no violation on remote access or the discussion request.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Aug. 19, 2025 workshop and regular meeting were held in a location inaccessible to people with disabilities.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by holding the August 19, 2025, meetings in a location that was inaccessible to members of the public with disabilities.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Committee did not provide remote access to the Aug. 19, 2025 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: we have consistently stated that a public body is not required to provide remote access to its meetings, so long as the meetings are held in-person at a location that is open and physically accessible to the public.

allegations.summary: Second complaint alleged the amended Aug. 19, 2025 meeting notice omitted the date and time of posting and of the original posting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law where both the original and amended notices did not conspicuously record thereon or therewith the date and time of posting.

allegations.summary: Second complaint alleged the Committee did not discuss a matter the complainant requested to be placed on the agenda.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to discuss any topic, nor does it establish requirements for the level of detail a public body’s discussions must include.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, including holding meetings in accessible locations and recording the date and time of posting on notices.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
